related_questions.question: How long to wait before taking a COVID test?

text_blocks.snippet: If you have COVID-19 symptoms, test immediately. If you were exposed and have no symptoms, wait at least 5 full days after exposure before testing, according to the FDA. If the first test is negative, follow the instructions for repeat testing, also from the FDA.
snippet_highlighted_words: If you have COVID-19 symptoms, test immediately.
If you were exposed and have no symptoms, wait at least 5 full days after exposure before testing

list.title: Symptomatic Individuals:
list.snippet: If you are experiencing symptoms like fever, cough, or fatigue, it's recommended to test as soon as possible.

list.title: Asymptomatic Exposure:
list.snippet: If you were exposed but don't have symptoms, waiting a few days is important because it can take time for the virus to reach detectable levels, according to the FDA.

list.title: Repeat Testing:
list.snippet: Some tests, especially antigen tests, may require repeat testing after a negative result to confirm the absence of infection, notes the FDA.

list.title: Test Type:
list.snippet: The time it takes to detect the virus can vary between different COVID-19 variants and different types of tests, according to the FDA.

list.title: Contagiousness:
list.snippet: It's important to note that you can be contagious even before a positive test result, especially in the initial days after exposure, according to the FDA.
